sections.title: Introduction to Views
content: AMPS Views are high-performance virtual topics that aggregate or transform data from one or more underlying SOW topics.
They are similar to 'Materialized Views' in traditional databases, but they update in real-time as the underlying data changes.
Views allow for complex calculations, filtering, and joining of data before it ever reaches the subscriber.

sections.title: Aggregation Functions
content: AMPS supports standard SQL-like aggregation functions to summarize data streams.
Key functions include: SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, COUNT, and COUNT_DISTINCT.
The ANY function can also be used to retrieve an arbitrary value from a group.
Grouping is achieved by specifying non-aggregated fields in the view definition, effectively creating a 'GROUP BY' structure.

sections.title: Joining Topics
content: Views can perform joins across multiple topics, even if they use different message types (e.g., joining FIX with JSON).
AMPS primarily uses LEFT OUTER JOIN semantics: if a match is not found in the joined topic, NULL values are projected for those fields.
Joins are string-based by default, so care must be taken with numeric formats (e.g., '10' vs '10.0').

sections.title: Conflation
content: Conflation helps subscribers handle high-velocity data by limiting the update rate.
Time-based conflation sends the latest state of a record at regular intervals (e.g., every 1s).
Subscription-based conflation allows individual clients to request their own intervals.
Topic-based conflation is defined on the server and applies to all subscribers of that topic.

sections.title: Out-of-Focus (OOF) Notifications
content: OOF notifications inform a subscriber when a record no longer matches their filter criteria.
This happens when a record is deleted, expires, or is updated such that it no longer meets the filter.
OOF messages include a 'reason' header (deleted, expired, filter, entitlement) to help the application take appropriate action.
